summary.title: How a 64k intro is made
summary.one_liner: A post-mortem of the 64k demoscene intro "Guberniya" showing how a small real-time demo was built with C++, OpenGL, raymarching, custom post-processing, and a self-made paulstretch-style music pipeline.
takeaways: How a 64k demo is structured: scrapping the standard library, compressing the binary with kkrunchy, and loading only needed OpenGL functions.
How raymarched terrain and SDF models are built, including analytic derivatives for faster ray stepping and soft shadows.
How the post-processing chain (DOF, bloom, lens flares, FXAA, colour grading, film grain) is assembled, and how live shader reloading and Rocket sync speed up iteration.
How the music was made without a VST synth: GPU-based paulstretch time-stretching feeding a MilkyTracker XM song using the gm.dls soundbank.
summary.summary: The author, cce, describes making Guberniya, a 62976-byte Windows 64k intro released at Revision 2017 by a six-person team in about four months. The article walks through the whole production: the C++/OpenGL codebase, live shader reloading, GNU Rocket keyframe sync, dear imgui tuning, and the decision to drop a unified lighting pipeline. It then covers rendering (mostly raymarching of SDFs and terrain), post-processing passes, the GPU-simulated wires and flock, and a music pipeline that combines a GLSL paulstretch and a tracker module. It is a dense, first-person developer post-mortem with code snippets and links to further references.
